newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Yields ended slightly up on Friday and the crown softened after an initial strengthening.

"We opened much stronger because U.S. and German yields closed lower and the German market opened strong. But then the crown weakened and the German market lost some of its strength," one dealer said.

Trade was relatively calm ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20 and the announcement of the Swedish government's stance on Europe's economic and monetary union, expected sometime between May 23 and May 30.
The crown weakened in quiet trade.
"We saw some trading by Swedish exporters in the morning. They bought marks against crowns and then we saw the same names buying back marks again," one dealer said.

The six month T-bill rate was unchanged at 4.19 percent and the ten year bond yield rose two basis points to 6.93 percent. The crown softened to 4.4740 crowns to the mark versus 4.4640 crowns on Thursday.
